A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PINNfluence. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.3 are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on three Navier–Stokes PINNs, including indicator scores, predictions, errors, and influence heatmaps.

after.justification: V2 retains these original PINN experiments and their results in Table 1 and Figures 1–6.

M1.justification: V2 adds a proposed PDE-parameter influence calculation using mixed derivatives (Appendix A.1, Eqs. 22–23), extending the perturbations the procedure handles. The trained PINNs, training-point attribution, and indicator calculations remain unchanged; OI is merely renamed RI.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same stationary 2D Navier–Stokes cylinder-flow problem. V2 mentions heat and Maxwell equations only as future applications.

E2.justification: Both versions compare the same good, bad, and broken PINNs against the same FEniCS reference solution. Quanda is newly cited for possible future evaluation, not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 3 retains the architecture, sampling procedure, training/test point counts, 100k Adam steps, and up to 25k L-BFGS steps. The PDE settings and DI/region-indicator definitions also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The wrong-physics and reduced-training-data comparisons, prediction/error maps, and spatial influence analyses are retained. Appendix A.3 contains the same supplemental analyses, with no additional robustness tests or ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 1 averages over test points in both versions.

E6.justification: All Table 1 scores and plotted results in Figures 1–6 are unchanged. For example, u1 DI remains 0.80/0.80/0.71 for good/bad/broken. Renaming OI to RI changes neither values nor rankings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the positive-definite argmin formulation with a nondegenerate stationary-point lemma, functional influence definition, theorem, and chain rule. It adds analyticity, continuation, and remainder claims, derives loss-weight/PDE-parameter sensitivities, and revises loss-removal normalization. Section 2 also reverses the prediction-difference sign to agree with the appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and main conclusion retain the same claims: adapting influence functions to PINNs, constructing heuristic indicators, and demonstrating their diagnostic usefulness on three Navier–Stokes models.

C2.justification: V1 claims parameter restrictions can always provide strict convexity and a positive-definite Hessian. V2 replaces that rationale with saddle-point motivation and explicit stationarity/nondegeneracy requirements. The cautions about expert-designed indicators and their inability to establish overall model correctness remain.

D1.justification: The implementation libraries, architecture, sampling and optimization details, and Appendix A.2 parameters are retained. The same code repository is disclosed in both; repeating its link in v2's abstract adds no new access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references supporting its theoretical treatment and future evaluation, including Schioppa et al., Dauphin et al., implicit-function theorem sources, and Quanda. Existing cited works and the main research positioning remain; publication-metadata updates are not additional works.

P1.justification: Appendix A.1 is extensively rewritten and reorganized from an argmin/proposition presentation into a general functional framework followed by separate perturbation cases. Main-text editing is lighter, including contribution bullets, clearer transitions, and OI-to-RI terminology.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from beside the conclusion into the Results discussion and receives RI headers. Figure 4 moves onto a separate appendix page, with surrounding layout changes. All six figures and both tables remain; the embedded plot images are identical.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the local stationary-point formulation and corrects the main-text perturbation sign. However, its new Eq. 13 requires r(epsilon)/epsilon^2 to approach zero after a first-order expansion, which is generally false even for analytic functions with a nonzero quadratic remainder. These substantive gains and the new theoretical defect leave the net quality direction unclear; the empirical evidence is unchanged.
